finding: The continuous-simulation example says every millisecond, which describes a numerical sampling cadence rather than the definition of continuous time.
handling: Questions distinguish the continuous model from discrete evaluation.

finding: The statement that simulation results are highly sensitive to initial conditions is unqualified; not every model has chaotic or strong sensitivity.
handling: Test that initial state can affect behavior, not universal chaotic sensitivity.

finding: High fidelity is illustrated as exactly matching reality, although the concept is degree of agreement and all models have scope limitations.
handling: Do not assert perfect universal fidelity; use intended-use agreement and stated simplifications.

finding: The slide names JetPack6.2.2, misspells Orin as Orion once, and gives apt install code_<version_name>_arm64.deb without explicitly marking a local path.
handling: Version questions are source-attributed. No installation is executed or treated as up-to-date operational guidance; use explicit ./ path if demonstrating a repaired local-file command.

finding: mkdir first_project is followed by cd my_project; sudo apt python3.10-venv omits install; python3 –m uses a typographic en dash. The claim that venv installs setuptools is Python-version-dependent.
handling: Questions explicitly flag/repair only named defects. Avoid claiming setuptools is installed by every Python version. No apt or pip actions run.

finding: The slide groups .py and .ipynb as scripts and lists an IDE as a need. A notebook is a structured container, not an ordinary .py script; execution need not require a graphical IDE.
handling: Distinguish notebook versus source file explicitly; do not require an IDE to execute every program.

finding: Gazebo/rclpy share a Robotics Sim box, but rclpy is a ROS2 client library rather than a physics engine; category membership is not exclusive.
handling: Frame category questions as the lecture diagram’s grouping; later bridge question distinguishes rclpy role.

finding: np.block uses a raw [[1]] leaf beside arrays, producing inconsistent list depths and ValueError. Comment Matrix multiply mislabels block assembly.
handling: Preserve exact-code failure. Separately label the repair np.array([[1]]) and explain assembled identity4. Later offset/norm evaluation is explicitly isolated or after repair.

finding: 100× faster and contiguous memory are unqualified claims: array views need not be contiguous and speedups depend on workload. Different shapes still require broadcasting compatibility; shown offset arrays have equal shapes.
handling: Do not accept universal performance/contiguity claims. Test array roles, valid arithmetic, and the compatibility qualification without claiming arbitrary shapes work.

finding: The integrate box labels solve_ivp/odeint as ODE/PDE solvers and the signal box mentions Kalman filters. These labels do not establish a direct generic PDE interface or a scipy.signal.Kalman API.
handling: Questions test named module roles and ODE use; do not invent a Kalman API. Broader API claims remain excluded pending specialist adjudication.

finding: The animation box promises30+fps without specifying hardware, workload or backend.
handling: Test FuncAnimation/blitting role, not a guaranteed frame rate.

finding: Velocity expression breaks after / without explicit continuation; parsing the literal displayed text raises SyntaxError.
handling: Explicitly repair with parentheses before evaluating finite differences. Example values are supplied in the question, not invented as unseen CSV contents.

finding: Table labels the HDF reader read_hdf5; tested pandas has read_hdf, not read_hdf5.
handling: Preserve source typo; no question presents read_hdf5 as a working API. Runtime attribute check retained.
Exact snippet raises NameError in a fresh namespace. Repair is stated before the returned distance is asked.

finding: Prior handoff alleged missing print-call commas. Direct inspection of all three print lines shows commas present; exact transcription compiles and produces the expected four lines.
handling: Do not label this source erroneous. Preserve the rejected allegation and executable trace for independent review.

finding: 90% task coverage,5–10 lines, any dynamical system, industry-standard wording and same-code sim/hardware assertions lack bounded evidence and assumptions.
handling: Test toolkit roles, acceleration mappings and sim-to-real practices. Exclude percentages, universal solver coverage and unconditional portability as general facts.
